question: Does a checked denominator-two fractional matching over all forced-conflict pair bounds strengthen the existing fixed-disjoint-pair headroom bound?
object: The complete 32-step forced-shortest-path conflict graph on each of the 20 existing exposed archive cases: 2785 pairs, including all 521 previously selected disjoint pairs.
pair_method: Reuse the exact SOL-aware pair-search source bytes from PR 6, including goal departures and safe capped-frontier bounds. Charge every pop and preserve unit conflict evidence.
aggregation: For each positive-edge connected component, solve maximum-weight assignment on the symmetric bipartite double cover. Extract numerator z_ij=[P(i)=j]+[P(j)=i], denominator 2, validate incident capacity <=2, and round each component's rational bound up. Validate assignment primal/dual certificates separately. Compare complete valid certificates by maximum, never sum overlapping alternatives.
development: Original maze-32-32-4-n128; fixed one-case pilot, no parameter tuning. Freeze implementation before the 20-case panel.
exposure: All inputs and prior results are published calibration data. No unseen transfer or new algorithmic novelty claim.
before_pilot: Price a favorable fully charged case using projected inherited pair costs as upper-bound weights, to see whether this aggregation can matter.
Check the double-cover/dual proof and distinguish fractional matching from integer weighted vertex cover and global MAPF optimum.
Validate assignment results/certificates against exhaustive tiny integer matrices, odd cycles, disconnected components and invalid witnesses.
Reproduce full conflict counts and the old greedy matching from the canonical published headroom scope.
verification: Use a separate pair cost-threshold verifier from PR 6 and a separate exact-integer aggregation checker. Validate IDs, canonical cases/full pair scope, capacities, component coverage, ceiling arithmetic, primal/dual feasibility, source/input hashes and journal completeness. Retain all caps, attempts and controls.
success: A stronger reproducible lower bound on at least one canonical case, without losing the prior valid fixed-matching alternative, or a precise null/obstruction with all evidence.
falsification: A bound above the inherited valid route, a tiny exact solution below a certificate, overfilled or aliased vertex capacity, wrong component rounding, noncanonical pair scope, or a failed independent pair-weight check rejects the result.
pivot: No alternate pair caps or tuned parameters. If aggregation does not improve the fixed matching, record the null result before considering a separately declared question.
authorship: OpenAI Codex gpt-6.1-sol author work, primary-source research agent and scoped review agents; not independent human scientific signoff.
